title: Dedicated capacity commitment matrix and contract playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Define a clear commitment matrix and contract playbook for Dedicated capacity customers that balances predictable reserved GPU pricing, controlled burst capacity, and pay-for-usage autoscaling. This ticket captures the proposed pricing bands, SLA tiers, standard contract terms, and a worked mapping to the enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) artifacts so Sales and Legal can respond quickly.

Goals: 1) Provide 3 commitment tiers with simple economics that scale from small pilots to multi-region enterprise fleets. 2) Define burst behavior and pricing so customers can exceed committed throughput without long procurement cycles. 3) Capture contract language and negotiation playbook for common concessions (SLA credits, data residency, audit-rights). 4) Map answers and required artifacts for the security questionnaire to speed RFP/SQ responses.

Success metrics: - Reduce average negotiation time for Dedicated deals by 30% within next quarter. - Increase conversion rate on outbound enterprise proposals by 15%. - Less than 8% of commitments require custom pricing by default.

Proposed commitment matrix: - Pilot Tier (S1): 4 reserved A5000-equivalent GPUs, 3-month minimum, effective committed discount 18% vs hosted list, $X per GPU-hour baseline (see pricing appendix link). - Growth Tier (S2): 16 reserved GPUs, 12-month minimum, 30% discount. Includes 2x burst capacity allowed for 24h per month at 50% of committed hourly rate. - Enterprise Tier (S3): 64+ reserved GPUs, 12–36 month minimum, 40%+ negotiated discount with SLA Tier options. Burst pool configurable, metered in GPU-hours; overage billed monthly.

Autoscaling and burst pricing model: - Warm autoscale buffer: included up to 10% of committed GPUs for instantaneous scale (no charge, short-lived) to maintain latency SLOs. - Burst credits: monthly pool allocated by tier (S1: 20 GPU-hours, S2: 400 GPU-hours, S3: configurable). Unused credits roll into a 3-month carry-forward. - Pay-as-you-go autoscale: additional GPU-hours beyond burst pool billed at negotiated overage rate (typically 50% of on-demand list but floor at committed hourly rate). - Billing cadence: monthly invoice for usage; committed portion billed monthly as amortized commitment.

SLA tiers and remedies: - SLA Bronze: 99.5% monthly uptime SLA, credits up to 5% ARR. - SLA Silver: 99.9%, credits up to 10% ARR, prioritized support. - SLA Gold: 99.95%, credits up to 20% ARR, named support, runbook integration. Standard playbook clarifies credit calculation, blackout windows, and canary/maintenance policies.

Contract playbook highlights: - Standard term: minimum commitment length by tier, auto-renew with 90-day opt-out window before renewal. - Data residency & access: include optional VPC/private deployment addendum for customers needing on-prem or VPC control. - Audit & compliance: define templates for SOC2 artifacts delivery cadence, and scope for in-person audits (limited, with cost recovery). - Negotiable concessions: short list (SLA credits, extended liability cap, custom reporting cadence, modest free burst credits). Avoid discounting below floor without cross-functional approval.

Security questionnaire (SQ) mapping: - Attached artifacts: SOC2 Type II report, KMS/HSM integration docs, network isolation diagram, pen-test summary, patch cadence doc. - Standard SQ language for Dedicated: prepared answers for 80% of common enterprise questions (data segregation, key management, logging, access controls). - Escalation: create an 'SQ fast-path' for Sales to request Legal/Security review with pre-packaged evidence bundle (link to Drive).

Trade-offs and decisions to be made: - Pricing simplicity vs. revenue optimization: we propose 3 tiers to reduce complexity for Sales but will leave wiggle room for S3. - Burst granularity: per-minute billing is more accurate but increases billing complexity; we opt for GPU-hour granularity for now. - Autoscale latency guarantees: offering instant warm buffer improves UX but increases capacity planning complexity for infra. ENG dependencies capture required telemetry and metering work.

Open questions: - Finalize numeric per-GPU-hour list price and negotiated floors (Finance input required). - Confirm whether burst credits should auto-top-up or be purchased as add-on. - Define detailed legal language for 'temporary overage' during DDoS or malformed traffic.

Links and artifacts: - PRD (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/dedicated-capacity-prd-2025 - Pricing appendix (sheet): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-pricing-appendix - Security evidence bundle (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/sq-evidence-dedicated - Example customer term sheet (Google Doc): https://docs.redwood.ai/d/example-dedicated-term-sheet - Billing integration GH spike: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6123

Acceptance criteria: - Finalized commitment matrix with numeric prices and discount floors approved by Finance. - Contract playbook doc with standard clauses and negotiation guidance checked into Confluence. - Security evidence bundle published in Drive and mapped to common SQ fields. - ENG tickets opened for metering, billing export, and autoscale telemetry with owners assigned.
